details: The cryptocurrency market is experiencing weakness following the U.S. midterm elections and the latest Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report. The Democratic Party's victory and the potential for a more aggressive Federal Reserve regarding interest rates are contributing to a bearish bias. Higher interest rates typically reduce market liquidity and decrease the attractiveness of risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Political Uncertainty, NFP Data Weigh on Crypto Confidence

details: Bitcoin traded around $75,700 on November 7, 2026, pressured by significant spot ETF outflows amounting to $1.28 billion, increasing odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike, and the lingering impact of a recent Binance hack. The cryptocurrency is currently on track for its fifth consecutive weekly loss, with major traders reportedly taking net short positions, indicating expectations of further declines.
title: Bitcoin Dips to $75,700 Amid ETF Outflows and Rate Hike Fears

details: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced new regulations effective November 5, 2026, requiring foreign-currency stablecoin issuers to establish Nigerian-incorporated entities, obtain local licenses, and maintain a minimum of ₦15 billion in paid-up capital. These measures aim to formalize the supervision and strengthen oversight of digital assets used for payments and foreign exchange within Nigeria.
title: Nigeria Imposes Strict Capital Requirements for Stablecoins

details: After an initial gain of $100 billion post-U.S. midterm elections, the crypto market has relinquished these advances due to a widespread sell-off in technology stocks globally. Bitcoin saw a 2.5% dip, XRP fell over 7%, and other major altcoins demonstrated broad weakness. However, some defensive assets such as Zcash, Tron, and gold-backed tokens experienced gains, suggesting a shift towards safer assets.
title: Crypto Market Drops $100B Rally Amid Global Tech Sell-off

details: Revenue for crypto wallet providers, including interface businesses, declined by approximately $700 million to $400 million in the first half of 2026. This significant drop is primarily attributed to reduced trading activity and volatile cryptocurrency prices, which have directly impacted fee income across consumer crypto businesses.
title: Crypto Wallet Revenue Drops $700M in H1 2026

details: A recent analysis by the Bank Policy Institute indicates that only two out of the ten largest dollar stablecoins, accounting for 26% of outstanding tokens, would meet the reserve requirements set by the U.S. GENIUS Act. This act, effective January 2027, aims to mitigate "de-pegging" risks by mandating that stablecoins are backed by highly liquid assets.
title: Most Stablecoins Fail to Meet US GENIUS Act Reserve Rules
